annotations.text:
Huddle marketing landing page.

Built on the app's own design system — same terracotta, same type ramp, same 4px grid and radii — so the site and the product read as one thing. Barlow is added for headlines because the wordmark is already Barlow.

Main (desktop) now runs on real product screenshots — retaken from the app, status bars trimmed — so it no longer carries a dark tweak (the shots are light-mode only). It has a Scroll reveal tweak instead (on by default): a tasteful fade-and-rise as each section enters view; browsers without scroll-linked animations fall back to a one-time fade on load. Mobile/Pricing/HeroSplit/HeroStatement are unchanged and still each carry a dark tweak.

No testimonials or logo walls anywhere: there are no users to quote yet, so the trust row uses facts that are actually true instead.

The 90-day window is the ONLY real gate. People, workouts, sets, offline and PRs all stay unlimited and free.

The footnote under the table is load-bearing — it's what stops the free tier reading as 'they're holding my data hostage'. Don't cut it for space.

'Import past workouts' is badged Coming soon because it genuinely doesn't exist yet.

DIRECTION A — product-first.

Why: the app is on screen in the first second, and for a tool this specific the product does the selling better than a promise does. It's also the safest at a phone width.

Tradeoff: it's the conventional SaaS hero, and splitting the width caps the headline at 70px so it never really shouts.

This is what the full desktop page is currently built on.

DIRECTION B — brand-first.

Why: full-bleed teal with a 92px headline and three product cards breaking the fold. Far more memorable, and it actually uses the deep teal from the logo, which the app itself never does.

Tradeoff: the product reads smaller and later, and this dark band competes with the offline section further down the page — you'd want to lighten that one if you pick this.
